stories.name: TSMC Chip Race Expansion
stories.blurb: TSMC is ramping up advanced packaging technology and raising prices to meet surging AI chip demand from Nvidia, Meta, and others amid intensifying competition with Intel.

stories.name: ASML High-NA EUV Deals
stories.blurb: Chipmakers TSMC, Samsung and Intel commit to ASML's next-generation High-NA EUV lithography machines, boosting ASML's stock and outlook amid surging AI chip demand.

stories.name: TSMC Revenue Surge
stories.blurb: TSMC's revenue and stock have been surging on strong AI chip demand, prompting analysts to debate whether the stock's rally reflects its true growth potential.

stories.name: TSMC in Global ETFs
stories.blurb: Coverage of international and emerging-markets ETFs, which often hold TSMC as a top component, comparing their performance and suitability for investors.

events.name: ASML inks EUV deals with TSMC, Samsung

4.text: TSMC reported strong A14 customer traction with tape-outs underway ahead of 2028 production, and plans to raise wafer prices 3–6% from January 2027 amid tight AI-driven capacity. Taiwan is building a Kaohsiung supplier-validation hub to shorten packaging qualification cycles, though it starts in three years with undisclosed capacity.

5.text: ASML's High-NA EUV tools are reaching more fabs, with partnerships involving TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and Nvidia. Coverage also compares ASML's monopoly position and valuation against peers like TSMC, Applied Materials, and Qualcomm.

6.text: TSMC holds over 73% of the pure foundry market and 90%+ of advanced AI chip share, spent $15.59B on capex in a quarter (up 42%), and will raise wafer prices 3–6% in 2027. Analysts remain bullish, citing AI-driven growth, expanding margins, and an undervalued stock.

7.text: ETFs holding TSMC are compared: FNDE, VXUS, VWO, VT, and URTH differ on costs and developed versus emerging market exposure. SMH, down 12% from its June high, is recommended for AI-driven semiconductor growth.
